sanskrit: nākālamattāḥ khagapannagāś ca; mṛgadvipāḥ śailamahāgrahāś ca nākālataḥ strīṣu bhavanti garbhā; nāyānty akāle śiśiroṣṇavarṣāḥ
english: Not out of season do birds and serpents go to rut, nor deer and elephants, nor the great beasts of the mountains; not out of season do women conceive in the womb, nor do the cold, the heat, and the rains come at the wrong time.

sanskrit: nākālato mriyate jāyate vā; nākālato vyāharate ca bālaḥ nākālato yauvanam abhyupaiti; nākālato rohati bījam uptam
english: None dies nor is born out of due time; nor does the child begin to speak before its season; not before its time does one attain to youth; nor does the seed once sown sprout out of season.

sanskrit: nākālato bhānur upaiti yogaṃ; nākālato 'staṃ girim abhyupaiti nākālato vardhate hīyate ca; candraḥ samudraś ca mahormimālī
english: Not before its time does the sun draw to its conjunction, nor out of season does it sink to the western mountain; not unseasonably do they wax and wane—the moon, and the sea with its garland of mighty waves.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam gītaṃ rājñā senajitā duḥkhārtena yudhiṣṭhira
english: On this point, too, men recite an ancient tale, Yudhiṣṭhira—the song that was sung by King Senajit when he was stricken with grief.

sanskrit: sarvān evaiṣa paryāyo martyān spṛśati dustaraḥ kālena paripakvā hi mriyante sarvamānavāḥ
english: This unconquerable cycle touches all mortals alike; for ripened by time, all human beings come at last to die.

sanskrit: ghnanti cānyān narā rājaṃs tān apy anye narās tathā saṃjñaiṣā laukikī rājan na hinasti na hanyate
english: Some men slay others, O king, and those in turn are slain by yet others; yet this, O king, is but a worldly manner of speaking—none truly kills, and none is truly slain.

sanskrit: hantīti manyate kaś cin na hantīty api cāpare svabhāvatas tu niyatau bhūtānāṃ prabhavāpyayau
english: One man thinks, 'He slays,' while another thinks, 'He does not slay'; but by their very nature are fixed the arising and the passing-away of beings.

sanskrit: naṣṭe dhane vā dāre vā putre pitari vā mṛte aho kaṣṭam iti dhyāyañ śokasyāpacitiṃ caret
english: When wealth is lost, or a wife, or when a son or a father has died, the man who broods, 'Ah, what misery!' only heaps fresh fuel upon his grief.

sanskrit: sa kiṃ śocasi mūḍhaḥ sañ śocyaḥ kim anuśocasi paśya duḥkheṣu duḥkhāni bhayeṣu ca bhayāny api
english: Why then do you grieve, when you yourself, in your delusion, are the one to be grieved over? Why do you mourn? Look how within sorrows lie further sorrows, and within fears further fears.

sanskrit: ātmāpi cāyaṃ na mama sarvāpi pṛthivī mama yathā mama tathānyeṣām iti paśyan na muhyati
english: Not even this self is mine, yet the whole earth is mine; as it is mine, so is it others'—seeing thus, a man is not bewildered.

sanskrit: śokasthānasahasrāṇi harṣasthānaśatāni ca divase divase mūḍham āviśanti na paṇḍitam
english: A thousand occasions for grief and a hundred for joy assail the fool day after day, but never the wise man.

sanskrit: evam etāni kālena priyadveṣyāṇi bhāgaśaḥ jīveṣu parivartante duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca
english: Thus, in their portions and in their season, the dear and the hateful—sorrows and joys alike—revolve among living creatures.

sanskrit: duḥkham evāsti na sukhaṃ tasmāt tad upalabhyate tṛṣṇārtiprabhavaṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥkhārtiprabhavaṃ sukham
english: There is only sorrow and no happiness—therefore it is sorrow alone that is truly felt; sorrow springs from the torment of craving, and what we call pleasure springs from the torment of sorrow.

sanskrit: sukhasyānantaraṃ duḥkhaṃ duḥkhasyānantaraṃ sukham na nityaṃ labhate duḥkhaṃ na nityaṃ labhate sukham
english: Hard upon pleasure follows pain, and hard upon pain follows pleasure; no one meets with sorrow forever, nor does anyone meet with happiness forever.

sanskrit: sukham ante hi duḥkhānāṃ duḥkham ante sukhasya ca tasmād etad dvayaṃ jahyād ya icchec chāśvataṃ sukham
english: For at the end of sorrows there is joy, and at the end of joy there is sorrow; therefore let him who desires lasting happiness abandon them both.

sanskrit: yan nimittaṃ bhavec chokas tāpo vā duḥkhamūrchitaḥ āyāso vāpi yan mūlas tad ekāṅgam api tyajet
english: Whatever be the occasion of grief or anguish or of sinking swoons of sorrow, whatever be the root of one's distress—let a man cast it off, though it be a very limb of his own.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṃ priyaṃ vā yadi vāpriyam prāptaṃ prāptam upāsīta hṛdayenāparājitaḥ
english: Be it pleasure or pain, the dear or the unwelcome, whatever comes, as it comes let him meet it with an unconquered heart.

sanskrit: īṣad apy aṅga dārāṇāṃ putrāṇāṃ vā carāpriyam tato jñāsyasi kaḥ kasya kena vā katham eva vā
english: Only behave, dear friend, but a little unkindly toward your wives or your sons, and you will learn at once who belongs to whom, and by what bond, and how.

sanskrit: ye ca mūḍhatamā loke ye ca buddheḥ paraṃ gatāḥ ta eva sukham edhante madhyaḥ kleśena yujyate
english: Those who are most dull in the world, and those who have passed beyond the reach of intellect—these alone flourish in happiness; it is the man between who is yoked to suffering.

sanskrit: ity abravīn mahāprājño yudhiṣṭhira sa senajit parāvarajño lokasya dharmavit sukhaduḥkhavit
english: Thus spoke that greatly wise Senajit, O Yudhiṣṭhira—he who knew the higher and the lower, who knew the world, who knew the dharma, who knew both joy and sorrow.

sanskrit: sukhī parasya yo duḥkhe na jātu sa sukhī bhavet duḥkhānāṃ hi kṣayo nāsti jāyate hy aparāt param
english: He who is happy amid another's misery can never himself be truly happy; for sorrows have no ending—from one is born the next.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ ca duḥkhaṃ ca bhavābhavau ca; lābhālābhau maraṇaṃ jīvitaṃ ca paryāyaśaḥ sarvam iha spṛśanti; tasmād dhīro naiva hṛṣyen na kupyet
english: Pleasure and pain, being and non-being, gain and loss, death and life—all these touch a man here in their turns; therefore let the steadfast man neither exult nor rage.

sanskrit: dīkṣāṃ yajñe pālanaṃ yuddham āhur; yogaṃ rāṣṭre daṇḍanītyā ca samyak vittatyāgaṃ dakṣiṇānāṃ ca yajñe; samyag jñānaṃ pāvanānīti vidyāt
english: The consecration for a sacrifice, the protection won by warfare, right governance of the realm through the science of just rule, the giving away of wealth as sacrificial fees, and true knowledge—let him know these to be the purifying things.

sanskrit: rakṣan rāṣṭraṃ buddhipūrvaṃ nayena; saṃtyaktātmā yajñaśīlo mahātmā sarvāṃl lokān dharmamūrtyā caraṃś cāpy; ūrdhvaṃ dehān modate devaloke
english: The great-souled king who guards his realm wisely and with sound policy, who is selfless and devoted to sacrifice, who moves through all the worlds as the very embodiment of dharma—he, when he has cast off his body, rejoices on high in the world of the gods.

sanskrit: jitvā saṃgrāmān pālayitvā ca rāṣṭraṃ; somaṃ pītvā vardhayitvā prajāś ca yuktyā daṇḍaṃ dhārayitvā prajānāṃ; yuddhe kṣīṇo modate devaloke
english: Having won his battles and protected his realm, having drunk the Soma and increased his subjects, having wielded the rod of justice over the people with discernment, the king who is spent in war rejoices in the world of the gods.

sanskrit: samyag vedān prāpya śāstrāṇy adhītya; samyag rāṣṭraṃ pālayitvā ca rājā cāturvarṇyaṃ sthāpayitvā svadharme; pūtātmā vai modate devaloke
english: Having rightly mastered the Vedas and studied the sacred treatises, having rightly protected his realm, and having established the four orders each in its own dharma, the king, his self made pure, rejoices indeed in the world of the gods.

sanskrit: yasya vṛttaṃ namasyanti svargasthasyāpi mānavāḥ paurajānapadāmātyāḥ sa rājā rājasattamaḥ
english: He whose conduct men still revere even when he has gone to heaven—townsfolk, country-folk, and ministers alike—that king is the best of kings.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca abhimanyau hate bāle draupadyās tanayeṣu ca dhṛṣṭadyumne virāṭe ca drupade ca mahīpatau
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: With young Abhimanyu slain, and the sons of Draupadī, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and Virāṭa, and King Drupada, lord of the earth—

sanskrit: vasuṣeṇe ca dharmajñe dhṛṣṭaketau ca pārthive tathānyeṣu narendreṣu nānādeśyeṣu saṃyuge
english: and Vasuṣeṇa who knew the dharma, and the prince Dhṛṣṭaketu, and so many other lords of men from diverse lands, all fallen in the battle—

sanskrit: na vimuñcati māṃ śoko jñātighātinam āturam rājyakāmukam aty ugraṃ svavaṃśocchedakārakam
english: grief will not release me, the slayer of my kinsmen, sick at heart, the cruelly fierce craver after a kingdom, the destroyer of my own line.

sanskrit: yasyāṅke krīḍamānena mayā vai parivartitam sa mayā rājyalubdhena gāṅgeyo vinipātitaḥ
english: He on whose lap I once rolled and played as a child—that son of Gaṅgā was by me, greedy for a kingdom, struck down.

sanskrit: yadā hy enaṃ vighūrṇantam apaśyaṃ pārthasāyakaiḥ kampamānaṃ yathā vajraiḥ prekṣamāṇaṃ śikhaṇḍinam
english: When I beheld him reeling beneath the arrows of Pārtha, shuddering as though smitten by thunderbolts, his gaze fixed upon Śikhaṇḍin—

sanskrit: jīrṇaṃ siṃham iva prāṃśuṃ narasiṃhaṃ pitāmaham kīryamāṇaṃ śarais tīkṣṇair dṛṣṭvā me vyathitaṃ manaḥ
english: that towering grandsire, a lion among men like an aged lion still tall, when I saw him strewn over with keen arrows, my mind was rent with anguish.

sanskrit: prāṅmukhaṃ sīdamānaṃ ca rathād apacyutaṃ śaraiḥ ghūrṇamānaṃ yathā śailaṃ tadā me kaśmalo 'bhavat
english: As he sank facing the east, dislodged from his chariot by the arrows, swaying like a mountain about to fall—then did a darkness of despair come over me.

sanskrit: yaḥ sa bāṇadhanuṣpāṇir yodhayām āsa bhārgavam bahūny ahāni kauravyaḥ kurukṣetre mahāmṛdhe
english: He, bow and arrows in hand, that scion of Kuru who for many days did battle with the Bhārgava upon Kurukṣetra in that mighty fray—

sanskrit: sametaṃ pārthivaṃ kṣatraṃ vārāṇasyāṃ nadīsutaḥ kanyārtham āhvayad vīro rathenaikena saṃyuge
english: he, the son of the river, the hero, challenged in battle from a single chariot the whole assembled warrior-host of kings at Vārāṇasī, to win brides—

sanskrit: yena cogrāyudho rājā cakravartī durāsadaḥ dagdhaḥ śastrapratāpena sa mayā yudhi ghātitaḥ
english: he by whose blazing weapon King Ugrāyudha, that unassailable emperor, was burnt up—he it is whom I have slain in battle.

sanskrit: svayaṃ mṛtyuṃ rakṣamāṇaḥ pāñcālyaṃ yaḥ śikhaṇḍinam na bāṇaiḥ pātayām āsa so 'rjunena nipātitaḥ
english: Guarding the moment of his own death, he who would not bring down with arrows the Pāñcāla prince Śikhaṇḍin—he was laid low by Arjuna.

sanskrit: yadainaṃ patitaṃ bhūmāv apaśyaṃ rudhirokṣitam tadaivāviśad aty ugro jvaro me munisattama yena saṃvardhitā bālā yena sma parirakṣitāḥ
english: When I saw him fallen to the earth and drenched in blood, in that very hour a most fierce fever entered into me, O best of sages—he by whom we were reared as children, he by whom we were guarded and kept.

sanskrit: sa mayā rājyalubdhena pāpena gurughātinā alpakālasya rājyasya kṛte mūḍhena ghātitaḥ
english: He was slain by me—greedy for a kingdom, sinful, a slayer of my elder, a fool—for the sake of a kingship that lasts but a little while.

sanskrit: ācāryaś ca maheṣvāsaḥ sarvapārthivapūjitaḥ abhigamya raṇe mithyā pāpenoktaḥ sutaṃ prati
english: And the preceptor, that great archer, honoured by all the lords of earth—I came up to him in battle and, sinful as I was, spoke a lie to him concerning his son.

sanskrit: tan me dahati gātrāṇi yan māṃ gurur abhāṣata satyavākyo hi rājaṃs tvaṃ yadi jīvati me sutaḥ satyaṃ mā marśayan vipro mayi tat paripṛṣṭavān
english: That burns my very limbs—the words my teacher spoke to me: 'You are a man of truthful speech, O king; if my son still lives, do not deceive me with falsehood'—so the brahmin, trusting in the truth, questioned me upon it.

sanskrit: kuñjaraṃ cāntaraṃ kṛtvā mithyopacaritaṃ mayā subhṛśaṃ rājyalubdhena pāpena gurughātinā
english: Taking an elephant as my screen, I played him false—I, exceedingly greedy for a kingdom, sinful, a slayer of my teacher.

sanskrit: satyakañcukam āsthāya mayokto gurur āhave aśvatthāmā hata iti kuñjare vinipātite kān nu lokān gamiṣyāmi kṛtvā tat karma dāruṇam
english: Wrapping myself in the cloak of truth, I told my teacher on the field, 'Aśvatthāman is slain'—when it was the elephant that had been struck down. To what worlds shall I go, having done so dreadful a deed?

sanskrit: aghātayaṃ ca yat karṇaṃ samareṣv apalāyinam jyeṣṭhaṃ bhrātaram aty ugraṃ ko mattaḥ pāpakṛttamaḥ
english: And in that I caused the slaying of Karṇa, who never fled in battle, my own most fierce elder brother—who is a greater doer of evil than I?

sanskrit: abhimanyuṃ ca yad bālaṃ jātaṃ siṃham ivādriṣu prāveśayam ahaṃ lubdho vāhinīṃ droṇapālitām
english: And young Abhimanyu, born like a lion among the mountains—it was I, in my greed, who sent him into the army that Droṇa guarded.

sanskrit: tadāprabhṛti bībhatsuṃ na śaknomi nirīkṣitum kṛṣṇaṃ ca puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ kilbiṣī bhrūṇahā yathā
english: From that day on I cannot bear to look upon Bībhatsu, nor upon lotus-eyed Kṛṣṇa—a sinner I, like one who has slain an unborn child.

sanskrit: draupadīṃ cāpy aduḥkhārhāṃ pañcaputravinākṛtām śocāmi pṛthivīṃ hīnāṃ pañcabhiḥ parvatair iva
english: And Draupadī too, who deserved no sorrow, now bereft of her five sons—I grieve for her, as for the earth stripped of its five mountains.

sanskrit: so 'ham āgaskaraḥ pāpaḥ pṛthivīnāśakārakaḥ āsīna evam evedaṃ śoṣayiṣye kalevaram
english: So I, the wrongdoer, the sinner, the cause of the earth's ruin, shall sit here even thus and waste away this body of mine.

sanskrit: prāyopaviṣṭaṃ jānīdhvam adya māṃ gurughātinam jātiṣv anyāsv api yathā na bhaveyaṃ kulāntakṛt
english: Know me from this day to have sat down to fast unto death, I who slew my teacher—so that in other births as well I may never again become the destroyer of my house.

sanskrit: na bhokṣye na ca pānīyam upayokṣye kathaṃ cana śoṣayiṣye priyān prāṇān ihastho 'haṃ tapodhana
english: I will not eat, nor will I in any wise take water; I will wither away the dear breath of my life, staying here, O you whose wealth is austerity.

sanskrit: yatheṣṭaṃ gamyatāṃ kāmam anujāne prasādya vaḥ sarve mām anujānīta tyakṣyāmīdaṃ kalevaram
english: Go now wherever you please; I freely give you leave, having made my peace with you. Grant me, all of you, your leave in turn—I shall cast off this body.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tam evaṃvādinaṃ pārthaṃ bandhuśokena vihvalam maivam ity abravīd vyāso nigṛhya munisattamaḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: To Pārtha as he spoke thus, overwhelmed with grief for his kinsmen, Vyāsa, the best of sages, restraining him, said, 'Not so!'

sanskrit: ativelaṃ mahārāja na śokaṃ kartum arhasi punar uktaṃ pravakṣyāmi diṣṭam etad iti prabho
english: Beyond all measure, great king, you ought not to grieve. Once more I shall declare it to you, O lord: this was ordained by fate.

sanskrit: saṃyogā viprayogāś ca jātānāṃ prāṇināṃ dhruvam budbudā iva toyeṣu bhavanti na bhavanti ca
english: Unions and separations are the certain lot of all born creatures; like bubbles upon the waters, they come into being and pass away.

sanskrit: sarve kṣayāntā nicayāḥ patanāntāḥ samucchrayāḥ saṃyogā viprayogāntā maraṇāntaṃ hi jīvitam
english: All that is heaped up ends in wasting away; all that rises up ends in falling; all unions end in separation, and life itself ends in death.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ duḥkhāntam ālasyaṃ dākṣyaṃ duḥkhaṃ sukhodayam bhūtiḥ śrīr hrīr dhṛtiḥ siddhir nādakṣe nivasanty uta
english: Pleasure ends in pain, and so does sloth; diligence is painful, yet it gives rise to happiness; prosperity, fortune, modesty, steadfastness, and success do not dwell with the slothful.

sanskrit: nālaṃ sukhāya suhṛdo nālaṃ duḥkhāya durhṛdaḥ na ca prajñālam arthebhyo na sukhebhyo 'py alaṃ dhanam
english: Friends cannot suffice to make one happy, nor enemies to make one wretched; wisdom does not suffice to win wealth, nor does wealth suffice to win happiness.

sanskrit: yathā sṛṣṭo 'si kaunteya dhātrā karmasu tat kuru ata eva hi siddhis te neśas tvam ātmanā nṛpa
english: As you were created by the Ordainer for your works, son of Kuntī, so perform them; for from that alone comes your success—you are not your own master, O king.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca jñātiśokābhitaptasya prāṇān abhyutsisṛkṣataḥ jyeṣṭhasya pāṇḍuputrasya vyāsaḥ śokam apānudat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As the eldest son of Pāṇḍu, scorched by grief for his kinsmen, was minded to give up his life, Vyāsa drove away his sorrow.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam aśmagītaṃ naravyāghra tan nibodha yudhiṣṭhira
english: Vyāsa said: On this point, too, men recite an ancient tale, the song of Aśman, O tiger among men; hear it, Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: aśmānaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ prājñaṃ vaideho janako nṛpaḥ saṃśayaṃ paripapraccha duḥkhaśokapariplutaḥ
english: King Janaka of Videha, plunged in pain and grief, questioned upon his doubt the wise brahmin Aśman.

sanskrit: janaka uvāca āgame yadi vāpāye jñātīnāṃ draviṇasya ca nareṇa pratipattavyaṃ kalyāṇaṃ katham icchatā
english: Janaka said: In the coming or the going of kinsmen and of wealth, how should a man who desires his own welfare bear himself?

sanskrit: aśmovāca utpannam imam ātmānaṃ narasyānantaraṃ tataḥ tāni tāny abhivartante duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca
english: Aśman said: From the very moment a man's self comes into being, straightway thereafter these manifold sorrows and joys come upon him.

sanskrit: teṣām anyatarāpattau yad yad evopasevate tat tad dhi cetanām asya haraty abhram ivānilaḥ
english: And when one or another of these befalls him, whatever he then resorts to carries off his understanding, as the wind sweeps away a cloud.

sanskrit: abhijāto 'smi siddho 'smi nāsmi kevalamānuṣaḥ ity evaṃ hetubhis tasya tribhiś cittaṃ prasicyati
english: 'I am nobly born, I am accomplished, I am no mere common man'—by these three grounds is a man's mind flooded with conceit.

sanskrit: sa prasiktamanā bhogān visṛjya pitṛsaṃcitān parikṣīṇaḥ parasvānām ādānaṃ sādhu manyate
english: His mind thus overflowing, he squanders the enjoyments his fathers amassed, and once impoverished he comes to think it well to seize the goods of others.

sanskrit: tam atikrāntamaryādam ādadānam asāṃpratam pratiṣedhanti rājāno lubdhā mṛgam iveṣubhiḥ
english: Him, transgressing all bounds and grasping at what is not his due, kings hold back—as hunters hold back a deer with their arrows.

sanskrit: ye ca viṃśativarṣā vā triṃśadvarṣāś ca mānavāḥ pareṇa te varṣaśatān na bhaviṣyanti pārthiva
english: Those men who are twenty years of age, or thirty, will not endure beyond a hundred years, O king.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ paramaduḥkhānāṃ buddhyā bheṣajam ādiśet sarvaprāṇabhṛtāṃ vṛttaṃ prekṣamāṇas tatas tataḥ
english: For these most grievous sorrows let a man prescribe a remedy by his understanding, regarding all the while, here and there, the lot of every living creature that bears breath.

sanskrit: mānasānāṃ punar yonir duḥkhānāṃ cittavibhramaḥ aniṣṭopanipāto vā tṛtīyaṃ nopapadyate
english: The source of mental sorrows is the bewilderment of the mind, or the onset of what is unwished-for; a third cause there is not.

sanskrit: evam etāni duḥkhāni tāni tānīha mānavam vividhāny upavartante tathā sāṃsparśakāni ca
english: Thus do these sorrows, of every kind, come upon a man here, and so too do those that arise from bodily contact.

sanskrit: jarāmṛtyū ha bhūtāni khāditārau vṛkāv iva balināṃ durbalānāṃ ca hrasvānāṃ mahatām api
english: Old age and death devour all beings, like two wolves—the strong and the weak alike, the lowly and the great alike.

sanskrit: na kaś cij jātv atikrāmej jarāmṛtyū ha mānavaḥ api sāgaraparyantāṃ vijityemāṃ vasuṃdharām
english: No man can ever escape old age and death, not though he has conquered this whole earth to the very shores of the sea.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ vā yadi vā duḥkhaṃ bhūtānāṃ paryupasthitam prāptavyam avaśaiḥ sarvaṃ parihāro na vidyate
english: Whether it be pleasure or pain that has drawn near to creatures, all of it must be undergone, helpless as they are; there is no turning it aside.

sanskrit: pūrve vayasi madhye vāpy uttame vā narādhipa avarjanīyās te 'rthā vai kāṅkṣitāś ca tato 'nyathā
english: In the first age of life, or in the middle, or in the last, O lord of men, these conditions are not to be shunned, yet the things one longs for turn out otherwise.

sanskrit: supriyair viprayogaś ca saṃprayogas tathāpriyaiḥ arthānarthau sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ vidhānam anuvartate
english: Parting from the well-beloved, and union with the unloved, gain and loss, pleasure and pain—all follow the appointed ordinance.

sanskrit: prādurbhāvaś ca bhūtānāṃ dehanyāsas tathaiva ca prāptivyāyāmayogaś ca sarvam etat pratiṣṭhitam
english: The coming-forth of beings, and likewise the laying-down of the body, and the toil of effort by which men obtain things—all this is fixed and ordained.

sanskrit: gandhavarṇarasasparśā nivartante svabhāvataḥ tathaiva sukhaduḥkhāni vidhānam anuvartate
english: Smell, colour, taste, and touch arise and cease by their own nature; even so do pleasures and pains follow the appointed ordinance.

sanskrit: āsanaṃ śayanaṃ yānam utthānaṃ pānabhojanam niyataṃ sarvabhūtānāṃ kālenaiva bhavanty uta
english: Sitting, lying down, going, rising up, drinking, and eating—all are fixed for every living creature, and come to pass by time alone.
